name: Deepak Fertilisers & Petrochemicals Corporation Ltd
title: Deepak Fertilisers & Petrochemicals Corporation Ltd - 500645 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Record Q1 operating EBITDA of INR845 crore (26% margin) on TAN and ammonia price strength; two new capacities (Gopalpur TAN, Dahej nitric acid) due to start in Q2 FY27, within approved capex of INR3,850 crore spent.

summary.headline: Deepak Fertilisers Q1 FY27 operating EBITDA hit record INR845 crore (+65% YoY) at 26% margin; PAT INR490 crore (+101% YoY).
summary.overview:
Revenue rose 22% YoY to INR3,256 crore, with operating EBITDA up 65% YoY and 139% QoQ to a record INR845 crore. Margin expanded to 26% from 19% a year ago and about 12% in Q4 FY26, driven by stronger TAN, nitric acid and IPA realisations plus early benefits of Equinor LNG supply, which began with the first cargo in May. Net debt fell to INR4,719 crore and debt/EBITDA improved to 1.4x despite over INR500 crore of quarterly capex. Gopalpur TAN (about 96% complete) and Dahej nitric acid (about 93% complete) are expected to start operations in Q2 FY27, within the approved capex envelope of about INR3,850 crore spent to date.</overview>

segments.name: Mining chemicals (TAN)
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR911 crore (+37% YoY) on volume of 130 KT, which was lower due to a few days of supply-chain disruption from new PESO guidelines. B2C revenue grew 42% to INR151 crore, 17% of segment revenue.

segments.name: Industrial chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR490 crore. Merchant nitric acid sales flat at around 80 KT YoY. IPA volumes hit by propylene availability constraints, though pharma-grade demand and realisations supported profit.

segments.name: Crop nutrition
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR1,367 crore (+9% YoY) despite delayed monsoon, high input costs and subsidy misalignment. Manufactured NPK sales +4%; specialty and Croptek products are 43% of segment revenue.

guidance_outlook: Gopalpur TAN and Dahej nitric acid projects expected to commence operations in Q2 FY27; management said they should be operational around end of the quarter.
Management expects faster ramp-up for the new plants (same chemistry, not new technology); analyst's ~80% utilisation for Q4 FY27 was not explicitly confirmed.
Equinor LNG savings described as sizable; a figure of around INR300 crore was cited by an analyst, and management said current conditions support that level but it could rise or fall.
Phase-out of legacy gas contracts to complete by Q4 FY27, after which Equinor supply is expected to be sufficient for all requirements.
Management declined to guide full-year EBITDA margin, calling it too early; said the new capacities and gas benefits will lift the base by year-end.
Q2 expected to see a seasonal slowdown in mining from monsoon, with a pick-up in crop nutrition demand after good rains.
Ammonia prices expected to stay elevated for at least some more quarters; ammonia FOB Middle East around USD600/t.
Net debt expected to peak near current levels (about INR4,700-4,800 crore) before deleveraging begins this year.
capex_capacity: Gopalpur TAN project about 96% complete; Dahej nitric acid project about 93% complete; both expected to start operations in Q2 FY27.
Total capex spent till Q1 about INR3,850 crore, within approved envelope.

Ammonia plant averaged 94% utilisation in Q1; April had gas constraints, but supply normalised after May with Equinor. Debottlenecking yielded about 10% capacity improvement, with the plant running at about 5 lakh tonnes.
Ammonia for Gopalpur to be bought externally; the other three captive businesses at Taloja use captive ammonia. About 80% of ammonia is captive consumption.
New plants to be depreciated over 25 years.
Explosives acquisition (DMSL) completed in May 2026; facility being upgraded with new explosives plants planned.
demand_pricing: TAN and ammonia prices remain elevated due to the Middle East conflict but have softened from war peaks, which management said was factored in.
Analyst flagged possible Russian FGAN export ban from October 2026, per global analysts; management did not confirm.
Management sees market growing 6-7% p.a.; even with new capacity, the market is expected to stay roughly balanced to short over the medium term.
Nitric acid pricing improved on supply tightness and lower imports; merchant nitric acid volumes flat YoY.
Raw-material pressure expected in crop nutrition (phos acid, sulphur) with the need for faster government subsidy corrections.
Management said elevated margins in TAN are expected to persist near term, with medium-to-long-term margins returning to a consistent level.

qa_highlights.question: What was ammonia plant capacity utilisation in Q1 given gas issues?
qa_highlights.answer: Average 94% for the quarter; April had gas constraints, but post-May supply from Equinor resolved them. Debottlenecking gave about 10% capacity improvement.

qa_highlights.question: Why did TAN volumes fall YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Not a raw material, production or demand issue; a few days of logistics disruption from new PESO guidelines. Management expects normal volumes YoY from Q2 onward, with the monsoon seasonal slowdown.

qa_highlights.question: Is the DMSL listing going to be an IPO or demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: Committed in principle to list DMSL; form (IPO or demerger) not yet decided, with communication to the market later.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Equinor gas contract phasing in and what are the savings?
qa_highlights.answer: Legacy contracts phase out through Q4 FY27; Equinor to be sufficient for full requirement afterward. Savings described as sizable; an analyst cited around INR300 crore, which management said is broadly in line under current conditions but could move with crude, Henry Hub and international prices.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 EBITDA margins match Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to commit; said it is too early to estimate, though new capacity and full-quarter gas benefits will raise the base by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt near peak at around INR4,700-4,800 crore with some more debt possible during final project leg; deleveraging expected from this year as new capex contributes. Working capital needs are low, as the businesses are B2B.
